name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield falls towards 5.1% on 26 Nov, lowest since 9 Nov, after peaking above 5.35% on 16 Nov
state: The 10-year gilt yield fell towards 5.1% on 26 Nov, its lowest since 9 Nov, after rising above 5.35% on 16 Nov as markets priced a December Bank of England rise (Trading Economics). The monthly move is inside the 40bp Watch line and no weak auction or BoE intervention was found; Watch is kept under hysteresis while yields stay near multi-year highs, with risk easing.
for_you: Gilt yields feed into mortgage and borrowing costs. Households remortgaging and the public finances remain exposed to high long-term rates.
rubric_hit: Long yields near multi-decade highs (Watch); 10y monthly move < 40bp

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields surge as rate hike expectations mount

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
